 Judgment

Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation
amount of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.
Bhagyamma B V vs Zuno General Insurance

Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85675985/
1 2.

Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 29.06.2024 at about 12.45 am (early morning), she was traveling as a passenger in Tempo Traveler bearing Reg No.KA-06-AB-9701, in outer ring road,
opp. Vishal Mart, wherein the driver of the Tempo Traveler drove it with high speed,
rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Lorry from the behind and caused the accident.
In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

She was shifted to Vijayanagara Hospital, later shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient for the accidental injuries and spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards her medical expenses.
Petitioner stated that due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to perform her work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the she was hale and healthy and she is aged about 59 years and he was working as a cook and he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent no.2 who insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and the jurisdictional police have registered the Cr.No.132/2024 against the owner of two wheeler and Tractor and Trailer and drivers of the said vehicles and as such they are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.2 has not chosen to contest the petition and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through their counsel filed vakalath and their written statement by denying the entire petition in toto.
Respondent No.1 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the lorry.

Respondent No.3 being the insurer of tractor belongs to respondent No.4 has admitted issuance of the policy to the tractor and contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and they prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
4. Petitioner examined herself as PW-1, and MRO and orthopedic surgeon as PW-2 & 3 produced and marked 19 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 19 and they are fully cross examined.

5. Respondent No.1 has not chosen to lead the evidence, after obtaining sufficient opportunity from this tribunal and there is no material on record, to show that they are prevented from appearing before this tribunal and to lead their evidence.
Hence, their evidence is taken as nil.
6. I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides.
I have perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
Bhagyamma B V vs Zuno General Insurance Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85675985/
2 ISSUES 1.

2 ISSUES 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves that on 29.06.2024 at about 12.45 am(early morning), she was traveling as a passenger in Tempo Traveler bearing Reg No.KA-06- AB-9701, in outer ring road, opp. Vishal Mart, wherein the driver of the Tempo Traveler drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Lorry from the behind and caused the accident.
In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition.?
2 Whether respondent no.1 proves that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the lorry as contended at para 5 of the written statement.?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4.
What order
or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In the Negative  Issue no.3: In Partly Affirmative  Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  9. Issue No.1 to 3:- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW1 being the petitioner, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.

She has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch, IMV,
wound certificate, final report, police intimation, MLC which are at Ex.P.1 to 7, 15 & 16.
10.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents, it is evident that Manjunath.P.S S/o Srinivasa that is the son of the petitioner is the driver of the offending vehicle.

The final report,
sketch, Mahazar, IMV establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the actionable negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
11. In the cross examination of PW-1, she clearly deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle dashed against the tempo from the behind.
The final report is filed after thorough investigating, and it is not disputed by the respondents and it has attained the finality.
There is no material on record to disbelieve the version of the petitioner.
Further respondents have failed to establish their contentions as contended in the written statement.

Bhagyamma B V vs Zuno General Insurance Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85675985/
3 14.

sentences.text: Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary, inpatient record which are at Ex.P.7, 8, 9 & 17.

The aforesaid documents shows that the petitioner has sustained the left tibia fractures, CRIF with nailing is done to her on 06.07.2024 and she has taken treatment as an inpatient for 11 days and she has spent Rs.31,073/- for her medical expenses as per Ex.P.10.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
15.
Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 11 days.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the medical bills.
Accordingly the wound certificate, discharge summary, inpatient record, and the medical bills issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
Admittedly he has taken treatment for 11 days, for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, she might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.31,073/-, I award Rs.10,000/-.

In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.41,073/-
compensation under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
16. The petitioner has not substantiated her nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least 15 days lost her income.
Therefore I award Rs.8,250/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
17. The petitioner has examined the orthopedic surgeon as PW-3.
He deposed that, he has not treated the petitioner and he has physically examined the petitioner and verified the entire medical records, investigation reports.
He further deposed that petitioner has sustained the left tibia fractures, CRIF with nailing is done to her on 06.07.2024, and petitioner require another surgery for removal of implants.
In the cross examination he admit that there is no fracture for the fibula and petitioner is having arthritis as stated in Ex.P.9 and petitioner has lost her muscle power.
He stated that petitioner has 20% of whole body physical disability.
The oral testimony of PW-3 corroborates with the wound certificate, discharge summary and medical procedures and medical investigation reports of the petitioner.
Nothing worth is elicited from the mouth of PW-3 to disbelieve the physical disability assessed by him.
Petitioner has not established the fact that the physical disability is an hurdle for her earning capacity.

Further more,
the fact of percentage of physical disability is entirely different from the earning capacity.

Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body functional disability of the petitioner is assessed as 14%.

sentences.text: The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident, she has completed 60 years as per the entry in Adhaar card which is at Ex P.13.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "7".

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
18.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, she might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings due to accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- under this conventional head.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
19.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him due to accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- as compensation under this head.
As per the oral testimony of PW-3 petitioner require another surgery for removal of implants.
Tentatively petitioner is in need of Rs.30,000/- for additional surgery.
20. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl Particulars Amount  No.
 1 Towards medical expenses, attendant Rs. 41,073/-
charges, transportation, nourishing food 2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 8,250/- 3 Loss of income on account of Rs.1,94,040/-
permanent disability 4 pain & sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
5 loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
6 Cost of Additional Surgery Rs. 30,000/-
TOTAL Rs.3,13,363/-
21.
Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Liability: Admittedly the validity of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.1.
Further more, they have failed to establish the fact that insured has violated the policy conditions.
Accordingly Respondent No.1 being the insurer has to pay the compensation amount with interest.
Accordingly respondent no.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.
Accordingly I am answering Issue no.1 in the affirmative, Issue no.2, in the negative and issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
25. Issue No.4:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.3,13,363/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash shirestedar is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
